How the orchestrator reads his items (use these; if the code shows a better reading, say so in your notes):
1. Hold-LMB auto swing with the ONE-HANDED axes (hatchet «Топорик», axe «Топор»): after the player walks away the strikes keep landing on the old spot or somewhere else. The two-handed axe («Двуруч.») is right: find what differs (e.g. the feel-1 point-aim depth lock that keeps the strike target while the MOUSE barely moved must also release when the BODY moves; one-handed reach / arc / hand slot). Test: a bot holds LMB, strikes, walks / strafes 0.5-3 m and turns while holding; invariant: every strike lands where the current swing arc from the current body pose first meets material (never the stale point), for all one- and two-handed tools.
2. Branches stay when the stump is finished: branches (or branch items / bodies) that belonged to the part of the tree he chopped away stay floating or are left behind. They must fall with their part or drop to the ground as items. Test: chop a stump / low trunk with branches to the end; invariant: no branch of that tree without support after it, items count conserved.
3. Cutting the stump top: the piece that falls off is a perfect cylinder; it must carry the real cut geometry with every notch (its bottom = the stump's top cut surface, its sides = the trunk as it was). Test: piece mesh volume = the volume removed above the cut (+-2 %), and the distance between the piece's cut face and the stump's cut face <= one canvas cell.
4. Trajectory: replace the line look by ENTRY / EXIT holes: where the tool's strike shape goes into the material, where it would come out if the tool were infinitely strong («как по маслу»), and the hole between: red, semi-transparent, drawn on the front (entry) face and the back (exit) face, the inside part darker (it is behind material), visible through objects. Cheap (<= ~1 ms per frame in WebGL2, few draw calls); every tool. It must not jump while walking: test = walk straight / strafe at constant speed aiming at a trunk; the predicted entry point moves smoothly (frame-to-frame jump beyond the body's own motion <= 1 cm; save the series).
5. Stone texture swims / shimmers when a stone moves (carried, falling, fragments): the texture must stick to the stone (object space, not world space). Test: the texture coordinate at a fixed local vertex is the same before / after moving + rotating the body; browser shot pair.
6. Glass and ice shatter completely too easily. Study the physics FROM SOURCES (WebSearch / WebFetch; cite them in notes): brittle fracture (Griffith / Irwin, fracture energy G_c = K_IC^2 / E, K_IC of soda-lime glass, ice, quartz), the size effect, blunt impact on thick glass (Hertzian cone cracks), thin panes breaking in bending. Then make glass and ice (and quartz) behave like the stone class: a big block barely reacts to one blow (a local chip / cone, a crack); cracks spread over repeated blows; pieces break off where cracks join; a full split needs energy ~ G_c x the cross-section, so it scales with size; thin sheets and panes do shatter. Reuse the stone fracture path, not a separate shatter hack. Tests: 1 m ice block, 0.5 m glass block, 5 mm glass pane, quartz crystal vs hatchet / sledgehammer / god blows: number of blows to the first piece and to a full split, crack length per blow, with the source numbers in the notes.
7. Frame spikes / freezes when hitting brick and others, and even when just walking (web build). Find them in the browser (shader compile on first use, physics body or mesh creation, canvas / CSG rebuild, streaming, GC); fix (warm-up at load, spread work over frames, cache). Measure with a scripted walk + hits on brick / stone / wood / glass: per-frame script CPU and the count of frames with one job > 8 ms, before / after; plus wall frame time in the browser (SwiftShader is slow, compare like with like).
8. Stone pieces that break off stay fixed or move toward the blow. A share of the blow energy goes into kinetic energy: pieces fly off a little, away from the hit (along the blow and the outward face normal); small pieces further, big slabs tip. Deterministic. Test: N breaks on several stones: every piece's initial velocity points away from the tool (dot > 0) and 1/2 m v^2 matches the chosen energy share (+-10 %).
9. The delay between the hit and the break: measure contact frame -> visible change (frames, ms) in solo and 2-process; cut it to the contact frame where possible: pre-compute the carve / fracture for the predicted contact during the wind-up (LMB held) and apply on contact; the server stays the authority (a different server result corrects the visual). Test: frames from contact to the visible change, before / after, solo and 2-process.
10. Shovel load: switching from the shovel to the bare hand moves the soil into the hand. The load belongs to the TOOL: it stays on the shovel when switching hands / slots and in the inventory, and the shovel shows it there. The load is a composition: litres per material (soil, gravel, turf / grass, sand, clay...) shown separately in the HUD and the item panel; dumping puts back each material (mass conserved per material). Tests: dig 8 L, switch to the hand -> hand empty, back -> 8 L; into the inventory and back -> 8 L; a mixed dig -> per-material litres sum to the total, conserved on dump.
11. Water sounds missing in places: find water (river, lake, pools, range troughs, liquids) without ambient / footstep / splash sound; fix with one cheap system (distance-culled emitters along water, steps in shallow water, splash when things fall in). Test: a bot visits every water kind and checks a sound would play there (headless: the emitter / player is active within its range).
12. Every 3D tool and item mesh (hands, tools of every shape x material, items, pieces) has no holes: a headless test checks watertightness (each edge shared by exactly two triangles with opposite winding, no degenerate triangles, normals outward) and shots of each tool from a few angles; fix the holes it finds.
13. Ground texture: square grass / dirt edges after digging (img2) and blocky grass patches on heaps (img3). Find the cause; fix it only if the fix is small and safe (e.g. mask filtering / edge noise); a full layered ground is a later design wave, so otherwise write the cause and numbers in your notes. Test: max colour / alpha jump across dig-cell borders on dug, regrown and heap ground (extend the feel-1 item 18 check).

extends Node3D
## feel-2 L1 (item 14): random hits on real rocks until a count is reached, CSG inputs dumped before every call so a native
## crash (signal 11) leaves the call that caused it. Run in a fresh process per seed (csg_stress.sh counts the crashes):
##   godot --headless --path . res://world/stone/csg_stress.tscn -- seed=1 rocks=6 hits=40 [dump=<abs path>]
## Lines: CSGS_HIT <n> (flushed), CSGS_DONE hits=N csg_ops=M folds=F refused=R balance=B.
var _seed := 1
var _hits := 0


func _arg(k: String, d: String) -> String:
	for a in OS.get_cmdline_user_args():
		if a.begins_with(k + "="):
			return a.substr(k.length() + 1)
	return d


func _ready() -> void:
	Engine.set_meta("autotest", true)
	_run.call_deferred()


func _run() -> void:
	await get_tree().process_frame
	_seed = int(_arg("seed", "1"))
	StoneMesh.dump_path = _arg("dump", "")
	var rng := RandomNumberGenerator.new()
	rng.seed = _seed
	var n_rocks := int(_arg("rocks", "6"))
	var n_hits := int(_arg("hits", "40"))
	var kinds := ["granite", "sandstone", "limestone", "flint", "concrete", "brick"]
	var worst_bal := 0.0
	for b in n_rocks:
		var r := RockNode.new()
		var kind: String = kinds[rng.randi() % kinds.size()]
		r.setup(995000 + _seed * 100 + b, kind, 500 + _seed * 7 + b * 13,
			Basis.from_euler(Vector3(b, b * 2, _seed)).scaled(Vector3.ONE * (0.5 + 0.1 * (b % 4))))
		r.position = Vector3(b * 3.0, 0.0, 120.0)
		add_child(r)
		await get_tree().process_frame
		var v0 := r.volume
		var chips := 0.0
		var ch_v := 0.0
		var tool := Tools.make([4, 5, 1, 3][rng.randi() % 4], [4, 5][rng.randi() % 2], 1)
		for h in n_hits:
			var d := Vector3(rng.randfn(), rng.randfn(), rng.randfn()).normalized()
			var hit := RockNode.surface_hit(r.cells(), r.bounds().get_center() + d * (r.size * 3.0), -d, r.size * 4.0)
			if hit.is_empty():
				continue
			var e: float = Impact.energy(tool, Physique.at(h % 3), 1.0)
			var im := Impact.rock(tool, e, r.kind)
			print("CSGS_HIT %d rock=%d kind=%s h=%d" % [_hits, b, kind, h])
			chips += await r.apply_hit(r.to_global(hit.point), r.global_basis * hit.normal, -(r.global_basis * hit.normal),
				clampf(float(im.bite), 0.0, RockSystem.MAX_BITE), clampf(float(im.tip), 0.002, 0.05), float(im.energy),
				RockSystem.blow_force(tool, im), Callable(), e)
			while r.busy():

			_hits += 1
			for ch: Dictionary in r.last_chunks:

		r.queue_free()
	print("CSGS_DONE seed=%d hits=%d csg_ops=%d refused=%d folds=%d balance=%s" % [_seed, _hits, StoneMesh.csg_ops,
		StoneMesh.csg_refused, Fracture.folded, String.num_scientific(worst_bal)])
	get_tree().quit()

**Cause.** The fragile branch of `RockNode._break` used the raw blow energy and charged n pieces `R*a_ref*n`, with `a_ref` fixed by the card's shard count (roughly 2-7x too cheap for n<40). `count>=2` then turned the whole body into shards. - New `world/rocks/brittle.gd` with `Brittle.fragile_break(rock, p, n, e_into, e_raw, seed)`. It is called from the one hook line in `rock_node.gd` `_break`, which replaces the old `if c.fragile:` block.
- It uses G_c = K_Ic²/E (the card's `r`) and the stone class's CRACK_K = 8.
- A blow of crack energy E_c = 0.1·E_raw drives a crack s = sqrt((E_c + R·A_open)/(8R)). The body breaks only if that reaches the back face (or its thinnest extent, if smaller).
- The energy that breaks a cube therefore scales with its cross-section: 2x the edge needs 4x the energy. Ice cubes of 0.25, 0.5 and 1 m break at 11.2, 45 and 180 J, and 0.8x of the threshold never breaks them.
- A blow that doesn't break the body leaves 0.5·E_c/R of open crack in its mark, applied when the next blow comes. The stone path already uses that currency (`_damaged`, `_use_cracks`), so later flakes get cheaper.
- Past the gate, the energy left after paying the cone across pays n pieces by a grid-cut cost: a sheet gives up to 40 bits, a block barely over the threshold gives 2-8.
- Below the gate, the existing `_spall` makes the local chip. Quartz stays a stone-class card.

**Wanted**: `Branches._build` resumable in slices of <= ~2.5 ms. The smallest patch I see (GDScript coroutine, one code path):

```gdscript
static var slice_us := -1          # >= 0: _build gives the frame back (await) whenever it has used this many µs since the last await

		...                # tri_of[k] with 9 append_array per triangle): every N iterations
		if slice_us >= 0 and RockNode._now() - t0 > slice_us:
			await Engine.get_main_loop().process_frame
			t0 = RockNode._now()
```

Test: a bot holds LMB, strikes, walks / strafes 0.5-3 m and turns while holding; invariant: every strike lands where the current swing arc from the current body pose first meets material (never the stale point), for all one- and two-handed tools.
2. Branches stay when the stump is finished: branches (or branch items / bodies) that belonged to the part of the tree he chopped away stay floating or are left behind. They must fall with their part or drop to the ground as items. Test: chop a stump / low trunk with branches to the end; invariant: no branch of that tree without support after it, items count conserved.
3. Cutting the stump top: the piece that falls off is a perfect cylinder; it must carry the real cut geometry with every notch (its bottom = the stump's top cut surface, its sides = the trunk as it was). Test: piece mesh volume = the volume removed above the cut (+-2 %), and the distance between the piece's cut face and the stump's cut face <= one canvas cell.
4. Trajectory: replace the line look by ENTRY / EXIT holes: where the tool's strike shape goes into the material, where it would come out if the tool were infinitely strong («как по маслу»), and the hole between: red, semi-transparent, drawn on the front (entry) face and the back (exit) face, the inside part darker (it is behind material), visible through objects. Cheap (<= ~1 ms per frame in WebGL2, few draw calls); every tool. It must not jump while walking: test = walk straight / strafe at constant speed aiming at a trunk; the predicted entry point moves smoothly (frame-to-frame jump beyond the body's own motion <= 1 cm; save the series).
5. Stone texture swims / shimmers when a stone moves (carried, falling, fragments): the texture must stick to the stone (object space, not world space). Test: the texture coordinate at a fixed local vertex is the same before / after moving + rotating the body; browser shot pair.
6. Glass and ice shatter completely too easily. Study the physics FROM SOURCES (WebSearch / WebFetch; cite them in notes): brittle fracture (Griffith / Irwin, fracture energy G_c = K_IC^2 / E, K_IC of soda-lime glass, ice, quartz), the size effect, blunt impact on thick glass (Hertzian cone cracks), thin panes breaking in bending. Then make glass and ice (and quartz) behave like the stone class: a big block barely reacts to one blow (a local chip / cone, a crack); cracks spread over repeated blows; pieces break off where cracks join; a full split needs energy ~ G_c x the cross-section, so it scales with size; thin sheets and panes do shatter. Reuse the stone fracture path, not a separate shatter hack. Tests: 1 m ice block, 0.5 m glass block, 5 mm glass pane, quartz crystal vs hatchet / sledgehammer / god blows: number of blows to the first piece and to a full split, crack length per blow, with the source numbers in the notes.
7. Frame spikes / freezes when hitting brick and others, and even when just walking (web build). Find them in the browser (shader compile on first use, physics body or mesh creation, canvas / CSG rebuild, streaming, GC); fix (warm-up at load, spread work over frames, cache). Measure with a scripted walk + hits on brick / stone / wood / glass: per-frame script CPU and the count of frames with one job > 8 ms, before / after; plus wall frame time in the browser (SwiftShader is slow, compare like with like).
8. Stone pieces that break off stay fixed or move toward the blow. A share of the blow energy goes into kinetic energy: pieces fly off a little, away from the hit (along the blow and the outward face normal); small pieces further, big slabs tip. Deterministic. Test: N breaks on several stones: every piece's initial velocity points away from the tool (dot > 0) and 1/2 m v^2 matches the chosen energy share (+-10 %).
9. The delay between the hit and the break: measure contact frame -> visible change (frames, ms) in solo and 2-process; cut it to the contact frame where possible: pre-compute the carve / fracture for the predicted contact during the wind-up (LMB held) and apply on contact; the server stays the authority (a different server result corrects the visual). Test: frames from contact to the visible change, before / after, solo and 2-process.
10. Shovel load: switching from the shovel to the bare hand moves the soil into the hand. The load belongs to the TOOL: it stays on the shovel when switching hands / slots and in the inventory, and the shovel shows it there. The load is a composition: litres per material (soil, gravel, turf / grass, sand, clay...) shown separately in the HUD and the item panel; dumping puts back each material (mass conserved per material). Tests: dig 8 L, switch to the hand -> hand empty, back -> 8 L; into the inventory and back -> 8 L; a mixed dig -> per-material litres sum to the total, conserved on dump.
11. Water sounds missing in places: find water (river, lake, pools, range troughs, liquids) without ambient / footstep / splash sound; fix with one cheap system (distance-culled emitters along water, steps in shallow water, splash when things fall in). Test: a bot visits every water kind and checks a sound would play there (headless: the emitter / player is active within its range).
12. Every 3D tool and item mesh (hands, tools of every shape x material, items, pieces) has no holes: a headless test checks watertightness (each edge shared by exactly two triangles with opposite winding, no degenerate triangles, normals outward) and shots of each tool from a few angles; fix the holes it finds.

Find the cause; fix it only if the fix is small and safe (e.g. mask filtering / edge noise); a full layered ground is a later design wave, so otherwise write the cause and numbers in your notes. extends "res://world/rocks/latency_test.gd"
## Refuter (feel-2, item 9): contact -> visible change for the FRAGILE path (glass / ice break-through, shatter) and quartz / brick / concrete:
## normal path vs cut ahead (prepare with the very numbers), solo. Frames = engine process frames awaited by apply_hit until the last visible change.
## Run: godot --headless --path . res://.orchestra/tasks/62/feel2/refute/stone-glass/rf_lat2.tscn
## Lines: RF_LAT2 kind= form= E= normal_frames= vis= | ahead prepared= frames= vis= same_state=
func _ready() -> void:
	Engine.set_meta("autotest", true)
	RockNode.cpu_clock = true
	_go.call_deferred()


func _mk(kind: String, form: String, at: Vector3, id: int) -> RockNode:
	var r := RockNode.new()
	match form:
		"cube05":
			r.setup_solid(id, kind, RockNode._box(Vector3(-0.25, 0.0, -0.25), Vector3(0.25, 0.5, 0.25)), 0.0)
		"cube025":
			r.setup_solid(id, kind, RockNode._box(Vector3(-0.125, 0.0, -0.125), Vector3(0.125, 0.25, 0.125)), 0.0)
		"cube1":
			r.setup_solid(id, kind, RockNode._box(Vector3(-0.5, 0.0, -0.5), Vector3(0.5, 1.0, 0.5)), 0.0)
		"pane5":
			r.setup_solid(id, kind, RockNode._box(Vector3(-0.25, 0.0, -0.0025), Vector3(0.25, 0.5, 0.0025)), 0.0)
		_:
			r.setup_solid(id, kind, RockNode._box(Vector3(-0.12, 0.0, -0.06), Vector3(0.12, 0.09, 0.06)), 0.0)
	r.position = at
	add_child(r)
	return r


func _go() -> void:
	await get_tree().process_frame
	var cases := [["ice", "cube05", 5, 150.0], ["ice", "cube1", 5, 150.0], ["glass", "cube025", 5, 150.0], ["glass", "cube05", 5, 150.0], ["glass", "pane5", 0, 20.0],
		["quartz", "cube05", 5, 1500.0], ["brick", "brick", 4, 150.0], ["concrete", "cube05", 5, 600.0]]
	var n := 0
	var tot_a := 0
	var tot_b := 0
	var prepared_n := 0
	for cs: Array in cases:
		var tool := Tools.make(int(cs[2]), 5, 1)
		var e: float = cs[3]
		var im := Impact.rock(tool, e, cs[0])
		var ra := _mk(cs[0], cs[1], Vector3(n * 4.0, 0.0, 40.0), 8100 + n)
		var rb := _mk(cs[0], cs[1], Vector3(n * 4.0, 0.0, 44.0), 8100 + n)
		rb.rock_id = ra.rock_id
		rb.noise_id = ra.noise_id
		rb.fabric = ra.get_fabric()
		n += 1
		await get_tree().process_frame
		var pl := Vector3(0.03, 0.5 * (0.5 if cs[1] != "brick" else 0.09), 0.25 if cs[1] != "pane5" else 0.0025)
		if cs[1] == "cube1":
			pl = Vector3(0.03, 0.5, 0.5)
		if cs[1] == "cube025":
			pl = Vector3(0.03, 0.125, 0.125)
		if cs[1] == "brick":
			pl = Vector3(0.03, 0.045, 0.06)
		var nrm := Vector3.BACK
		var a := {"point": ra.to_global(pl), "normal": nrm, "swing": -nrm, "bite": clampf(float(im.bite), 0.0, RockSystem.MAX_BITE), "tip": clampf(float(im.tip), 0.002, 0.05),
			"energy": float(im.energy), "force": RockSystem.blow_force(tool, im), "raw": e}
		var f0 := Engine.get_process_frames()
		await _do(ra, a)
		var fa := Engine.get_process_frames() - f0
		var va: Array = ra.last_vis_frames.duplicate()
		await _wait_idle(ra)
		var b := a.duplicate()
		b.point = rb.to_global(pl)
		rb.prepare(b.point, b.normal, b.swing, b.bite, b.tip, b.energy, b.force, b.raw, true)
		var w := 0
		while not rb.prepared() and w < 4000:
			await get_tree().process_frame
			w += 1
		var f1 := Engine.get_process_frames()
		await _do(rb, b)
		var fb := Engine.get_process_frames() - f1
		var vb: Array = rb.last_vis_frames.duplicate()
		await _wait_idle(rb)
		var same := state_of(ra).replace(str(ra.rock_id), "") == state_of(rb).replace(str(rb.rock_id), "")
		tot_a += fa
		tot_b += fb
		prepared_n += 1 if rb.last_prepared else 0
		print("RF_LAT2 kind=%s form=%s E=%.0f mode=%s normal_frames=%d vis=%s | ahead prepared=%s prep_wait=%d frames=%d vis=%s same_state=%s miss=%s" % [cs[0], cs[1], e,
			String(ra.last_break.get("mode", "-")), fa, str(va), str(rb.last_prepared), w, fb, str(vb), str(same), rb.last_pre_miss.substr(0, 80)])
		remove_child(ra)
		ra.free()
		remove_child(rb)
		rb.free()
	print("RF_LAT2_SUM cases=%d prepared=%d normal_frames=%d ahead_frames=%d" % [n, prepared_n, tot_a, tot_b])
	get_tree().quit()
EOF

## Findings (things that do NOT hold)

### F1 (item 6, HIGH). Glass and ice slabs/blocks up to 20 cm thick still shatter whole from ONE ordinary blow
Repro: `... rf_brittle.tscn -- kind=pane2 place=mid` (log rf_brittle_pane2.log) and `kind=pane` (rf_brittle_pane.log), `kind=ice` (rf_brittle_ice.log), `kind=glass` (rf_brittle_glass.log).
Numbers (blow 1, 50x50 cm face, glass; weak hatchet 10 J, fit hatchet 20 J, weak sledge 60 J, fit sledge 150 J):
| body | weak hatchet 10 J | fit hatchet 20 J | weak sledge 60 J | fit sledge 150 J |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| glass slab 5 cm (31 kg) | 12 pieces | 34 | 40 | 40 |
| glass slab 10 cm (62 kg) | 4 pieces | 10 | 40 | 39 |
| glass slab 15 cm | holds, breaks blow 2 | 5 pieces | 31 | 40 |
| glass slab 20 cm (125 kg) | holds, breaks blow 5 | breaks blow 2 | 16 pieces | 40 pieces |
| ice slab 10 cm | 33 pieces | 40 | 40 | 40 |
| glass cube 25 cm (39 kg) | holds, breaks blow 8 | breaks blow 4 | 11 pieces | 40 pieces |
| ice cube 50 cm (115 kg) | holds, whole at blow 8 | 36 % flake at blow 1, whole at blow 4 | 11 pieces | 40 pieces |
Why it contradicts item 6: Maxim wants "a big block barely reacts to one blow", only thin sheets/panes shatter. Here a 62 kg glass slab breaks into 4 pieces from a 10 J hatchet tap and a 125 kg slab into 16-40 pieces from one sledge blow. The break-through gate is `thickness t <= sqrt(E_c / (CRACK_K R))` with E_c = 0.1 x blow: for glass at 10 J that is 12.5 cm, at 150 J it is 48 cm. Cause is the calibration (crack_share 0.1, CRACK_K 8, BANK 0.5: the brittle part's own notes call BANK "no source"), not a bug in the code path. The part's matrix only ran 0.5/1 m cubes and a 5 mm pane, so the 2-50 cm range was never tried.
Also non-monotone in place (brittle.gd + stone flake path): ice 1 m cube, fit sledge 150 J: blow 1 at mid-face takes a 35.3 % flake (353 L) and the cube is whole after blow 2; 4 cm from the side edge the same blow takes 0.06 % and needs 2 blows too (`RF_BR ice_100... sledge_fit place=mid/edge`). Weak sledge 60 J: 35.3 % at mid, 0.05 % at the edge. The brittle part knows the 35 % flake (its issue list); a 35 % flake from one blow on a 1 m block is the opposite of "barely reacts". Ice 0.5 m, fit hatchet (20 J), blow 1 mid: 36.1 % flake.

### F2 (item 8, MEDIUM). Shards of fragile bodies hardly move: kinetic share is taken from the small "into" energy
Repro: `... rf_kick.tscn` (rf_kick.log, lines `RF_KICK`, `RF_KICK_SUM`, `RF_KICK_CHECK rf_visible_motion ... FAIL`).
Numbers: 124 pieces over 44 blows of 12 materials/forms x 6 tools: 29 (23 %) start slower than 5 cm/s, 46 (37 %) slower than 10 cm/s. Worst: glass 50 cm cube, fit sledge 150 J raw: `into` = 7.5 J, kick = 5 % = 0.375 J for 26 shards, 19 of 26 start slower than 5 cm/s (they fall in place). Ice 0.5 m cube, fit hatchet: 39 pieces, 8 slower than 5 cm/s.
Why it contradicts item 8: "pieces fly off a little, small pieces further". For fragile cards `Impact.rock` into-energy is ~5 % of the raw swing, KICK is a further 5 % of that, so 0.25 % of the swing moves a glass shatter. (No piece at v = 0, none toward the tool, share = 5 % x into within 10 % in all 44 blows: those parts hold.)

### F3 (item 9, MEDIUM). The cut-ahead applies only to bit-identical numbers; any drift falls back to the full delay
Repro: `... rf_lat.tscn` (rf_lat.log). Prepared with the aim's numbers for a full wind-up, then the strike differs:
- energy x 1.0 and x 0.9995: prepared (3 of 15 each, only at offset 0); x 0.99, 0.9, 0.6, 0.3: prepared 0 of 15 each.
- aim offset 1 mm / 3 mm / 6 mm / 20 mm along the surface: prepared 0 of 18 each (offset 0: 6 of 18, the other 12 are the energy-factor-off cases).
Total 6 of 90 trials used the shadow; misses cost 1-3 engine frames on a 600 J pick blow on a boulder (granite/limestone/sandstone). The key​ is `_pre_args == args` with the contact depth snapped to 0.01 mm along the normal, so even a 1 mm sideways move on a curved stone changes it. `RockSystem._prepare` also assumes `Impact.energy(.., 1.0)`; a manual click that releases before full wind-up (any power < 0.995) never matches. `prepare_hold` is called only while LMB is held (`held_axe.gd:370`), so a quick tap gets no cut-ahead at all.
